---
argmap-version: 0.3
title: "Can We Govern Superintelligence? (Tang vs Shapira)"
author: "debate extraction round 1 (LLM-extracted from the episode transcript, single elicitor)"
date: 2026-07-19
source: "https://lironshapira.substack.com/p/can-we-govern-superintelligence-taiwans"
speakers:
  l: "Liron Shapira (host, Doom Debates; argues the Yudkowskian doom case), 2026-01-20"
  a: "Audrey Tang (Taiwan Cyber Ambassador-at-large; plurality / foomer-not-doomer case), 2026-01-20"
  s: "Audrey Tang, 2026-09-15: her post 'There is still time to reset the AI Doomsday Clock'"
  al: "joint: explicitly shared or conceded by both speakers"
  as: "joint: Tang at both dates, said in January and again in September"
# A display hint (2026-09-18, the third after D162 and D164): a later dated
# voice UPDATES an earlier one. The view for `s` keeps `a`'s lines: where the
# September post is silent, January stands; where she moved, both lines stand
# and the solve shows the clash. The January view is January alone, the
# pooled view is every voice. The solve of the map is untouched.
updates:
  s: a
focus: [everyone-dies]
# A display hint (D162): this map opens with the graph's "Fold links" mode on,
# so a folded speaker branch shows which other branch it touches. The reader's
# checkbox in the graph controls still wins for the session.
fold-links: on
# A display hint (D164): what a speaker DECLINED, on the record, to put a
# number on. In that speaker's view the listed claim shows a blank gauge and
# her words, never the value the solve finds for her mapped lines. Each entry
# needs a verbatim quote line by that speaker on that statement; the optional
# [^locator] picks the one the reader is shown. The solve is untouched.
declines:
  a: everyone-dies [^t012346], aligned-in-time [^t015009], doom-material [^t002247], foom-soon [^t011249]
related-maps: "iabied-comprehensive-en.argmap: shared statement ids reused where the proposition coincides (@everyone-dies, @whether-vs-when, @opaque); near-misses deliberately NOT co-named (@prepare-pause is the weaker debate analogue of the book map's @shutdown)"
description: >
  The Doom Debates episode "Taiwan's Cyber Ambassador-At-Large Says Humans &
  AI Can FOOM Together" (Liron Shapira vs Audrey Tang, published 2026-01-20,
  ~1h52m), extracted as the pilot of the multi-voice conventions
  (ideas/plans/archive/content-debate-tang.md). ONE map, TWO voices: statements
  are speaker-neutral propositions and carry NO pins (their posteriors come
  entirely from the mapped factors); every evidence is attributed to its
  asserter by id prefix ($l- / $a- / $al-), repeated as an "L: / A: / AL:"
  label prefix so attribution stays visible on the graph and outline surfaces,
  which show labels, not ids. Each evidence also carries a strength from that
  speaker's verbatim spoken register via the pre-registered R-SPOKEN table
  (AUTHORING_NOTES 2026-07-19 debate entry) and, since the 2026-09-12 pass, a
  `# kind:` key from the K-SPOKEN reading of the D161 rubric (AUTHORING_NOTES
  2026-09-12), which says how firmly the step is held rather than how likely
  it is. All rubric-derived strengths keep the `?` marker; bare numbers are
  reserved for numbers a speaker stated as numbers. A credence a speaker
  stated as a number sits in the statement's `# check:` slot (D39, D156),
  which the format gives ONE of per statement: where both speakers price the
  same proposition the second number stays in the trailing comment, and that
  gap is the map's standing argument for a two-author extension
  (AUTHORING_NOTES 2026-09-12 lists the three instances). Tang's REFUSAL of a
  point P(doom) ("the interval is the message") is carried by what the map
  does not author: no statement has a pin and no check slot holds a number of
  hers. The solve does not carry it. A credenceless statement still solves to
  a value, the arithmetic of the lines mapped into it, and that value is
  nobody's stated credence (until 2026-09-17 this paragraph promised the
  refusal "is rendered as blankness", which stopped being true the day her
  view got lines into the terminus). Verbatim spoken words sit on `>` quote lines with their transcript
  timestamp as the locator (D59), so the gloss reads as a claim and the words
  that carry it stay walkable back to the source. Every quote line opens with
  its speaker, "A:" or "L:", the way the line labels do: a statement is
  speaker-neutral and a joint line quotes both, so the quote's own voice is
  the attribution (the prefix is the map's, everything after it is the
  transcript's, verbatim). Five declared groups (D58)
  box the single-voice batteries, one speaker per box, so a reader can fold a
  whole case and see whose it was. Where the speakers concur
  NON-diametrically, the two-voice overlap discipline applies (AUTHORING_NOTES
  2026-07-19 addendum): full concurrence merges to one $al- line
  (author-the-weaker); subset claims split into a shared $al- part plus a
  single-voice residual re-elicited conditional on it; instance-of claims are
  rerouted to support the shared ground, so no agreed content is
  double-counted by the independent-factor accounting.
  Reading the solve: the whole-map solved value is a POOLED agent believing
  both speakers' factors at once, so it is neither speaker's credence and no
  node here should be read as "the debate's answer". The disagreement readout
  is the speaker view (2026-09-17): each speaker's own lines by id prefix plus
  every line they cite, solved on its own, in the editor's speaker selector
  and headlessly with `solve_map.py MAP --speaker`. A speaker view is not
  that speaker's credence either. Tang states no number for @everyone-dies and
  rejects the ten percent Shapira models for her ("I don't think so. No, I
  really don't think so"); of the fork she says "the probability of both, I
  don't actually know at this point, so that's my honest epistemic stance".
  The values her view finds on @everyone-dies and @aligned-in-time are the
  arithmetic of her mapped lines. Until 2026-09-18 every line of hers into the
  crux argued the good branch; her on-record grant of the bad branch is now
  her own line at the fork, $a-default-doom (not switching planes is
  "uncertain, but probably doom"; Felix's ruling on AUTHORING_NOTES 2026-09-17
  section 10, authored in the 2026-09-18 entry), so her view rests on what she
  granted as well as on what she argued. On @everyone-dies her
  view therefore shows NO number (the `declines:` hint above, D164): asked
  whether it still goes bad she answers "I literally don't know", and a view
  that carries her name must not print a figure she refused to give. The
  gauge there is blank and quotes her. The hint changes what is shown and
  nothing else: the solve keeps its value for the claim, the pooled view and
  Shapira's view show theirs. Since 2026-09-26 the same holds for
  @aligned-in-time: her 01:50:09 "the probability of both, I don't actually
  know at this point" answers Shapira's wrap-up question about exactly that
  claim, sits on it as a quote line and backs a second entry (Felix's ruling
  of 2026-09-26 on AUTHORING_NOTES 2026-09-17 item 5.3). The same day he
  ruled the other two refusals in: @doom-material (asked whether she will
  say doom is above one percent: "Because we don't know. We literally don't
  know.", 0:22:49), which her view also argues against through
  $a-material-uc, the ruling being that a claim can be argued and declined
  at once, and @foom-soon (asked for her ballpark timeline: "Well, it's
  literally not a number", 01:12:49). And a reader's override in the
  what-if lifts a refusal: the reader's number overrides it (declines.ts).
  2026-09-17 pass: the fork into the terminus has both halves, the joint
  $al-if-unaligned and Tang's own $a-if-aligned (Shapira never states the
  aligned half, so it is hers alone), and every ground a line rests on has a
  line of its own in the voice that asserted it (AUTHORING_NOTES 2026-09-17), so no
  statement floats at the reference fill and none is blank in the view of the
  speaker who asserted it.
  2026-09-18 pass: a THIRD, DATED VOICE. Audrey Tang's post of 2026-09-15,
  "There is still time to reset the AI Doomsday Clock"
  (https://au.civic.ai/p/there-is-still-time-to-reset-the), is extracted as
  speaker `s`, an "S:" prefix on its lines and quotes, with paragraph numbers
  as locators ([^p0915-NN]) since a written column has no timestamps. The
  `updates:` hint above says `s` updates `a`: her September view keeps her
  January lines (where the post is silent, January stands; where she moved,
  both lines stand and the solve shows the clash), the January view is
  January alone, and the pooled view is all three voices. She still states no
  number of her own, but she now relays and endorses the insiders' number
  ("more than 10 percent within the next decade"), so her September view SHOWS
  a value on @everyone-dies: the arithmetic of that testimony line
  ($s-breakwater) beside her January lines, and not a figure she gave. The
  `declines:` entries above are January's. Since 2026-09-26 a later voice
  INHERITS an earlier voice's refusals wherever it has no line of its own
  into the claim (declines.ts, Felix's ruling): her September view keeps
  the fork, @doom-material and @foom-soon declined, and prints its number
  on the terminus alone, which the post prices anew through $s-breakwater.
  The central September line is her own text against her own January step:
  $s-converged-no-coord weakens $a-converge (measurement makes coordination
  automatic) with the record of a converged and pledged field that is still
  unconstrained, "breaking the deadlock takes shared rules". Strengths in the
  September block come from the D39 written rubric (a column is prose, so
  R-SPOKEN's spoken hedges do not apply), kinds from K-SPOKEN as before. A
  proposition she asserts at both dates is one factor, never two: every
  September sentence that restates a January claim stands on its January
  line, listed in AUTHORING_NOTES 2026-09-18, and the block carries only what
  is new.

# ============================================================
# SPINE: the debate is meta-shaped. The doom proposition (@everyone-dies)
# is barely argued directly; the fight is over (1) whether a credence on it
# is even assignable (@priceable -> @doom-material), (2) the shared "can"
# axis both speakers grant (@ceiling-high, @rsi-plausible, @deadly-capable,
# @can-vs-will), (3) the crux: @aligned-in-time — Tang's plural/interpretable
# takeoff vs Shapira's no-iterations mainline — feeding @everyone-dies via
# the jointly-granted fork ($al-if-unaligned and, since 2026-09-17, its
# inverse, Tang's $a-if-aligned), and (4) the policy fork
# @prepare-pause vs @measure-then-sunset.
# Nesting: each cluster folds under its local conclusion statement; shared
# ground referenced across clusters stays a top-level cluster head (@opaque,
# the section-4 "can" axis, @dividends-needed, @oom-slices) so it cannot fold
# away with a cluster that borrows it. The one exception since 2026-09-17 is
# @post-attention: both its consumers sit inside folded boxes, so as a
# top-level head no drawn edge touched it in the default fold state and it
# drew as a parked chip with no gesture to un-park it. It is homed beside
# $a-switch under @arch-switch now, and $a-converge borrows it across boxes
# (one in-box edge, so no W6). Homing is nesting only: no relation changed. Since the
# 2026-08-03 spine-surfacing pass, the evidences that LINK cluster heads to
# each other are top-level too ($l-material, $a-material-uc, $al-foom,
# $al-can, $l-pause, $a-montreal, alongside the original $al-if-unaligned,
# its 2026-09-17 inverse $a-if-aligned, and since 2026-09-18 $a-care-route,
# the gardener block's route into the crux, and $a-default-doom, her grant
# of the bad branch),
# so the collapsed view shows the debate's shape instead of a wall of
# disconnected heads (spine test, W21); what folds under a head is its own
# intra-cluster support and objection traffic. Same-day tier pass: the
# Harari sub-debate (@slow-steers-fast and its lines) is consumed nowhere
# outside section 6, so it folds under @gardener-model and that block
# collapses to one card. The remaining heads are irreducible: the can-axis
# and @foom-soon are shared into @aligned-in-time's internal battle, and
# the rest are genuinely separate blocks (I2 listed nine until 2026-09-18
# and lists seven since: the four flags pass wired @xrisk-priority into
# $l-pause and the gardener block into the crux, AUTHORING_NOTES
# 2026-09-18). `focus:` declares the map's terminus (@everyone-dies), D57.
# Excluded as argumentatively thin (scope discipline, see FINDINGS round 5):
# the chips-geopolitics chapter, biography segments, most positive-program
# detail (Green Earth, 6-pack pack-by-pack, Softmax) beyond what carries
# inferential load. Transcript turn-label glitch 01:10:44-01:11:21 noted in
# FINDINGS; attribution there recovered from content.
# 2026-09-12 format pass: `# check:` on the three statements a speaker priced
# as a number, `# kind:` on all 45 strengthed lines (K-SPOKEN rubric, fixed
# before assignment, single pass, AUTHORING_NOTES 2026-09-12), and `>` quote
# lines carrying the verbatim spoken words each line rests on. Five declared
# groups (D58), one per single-voice battery, replace the `# --` banner
# comments no tool could see: three in the credence dispute (::nan-case,
# ::ballpark-case, ::glass-condition) and two at the crux (::tang-routes,
# ::shapira-record). Each is nested rather than document-level, so the W12
# whole-block rule does not bite, and each folds to a summary card.
# The 15 premise-less direct-assertion floors are unchanged and draw the I4
# reading note by design. Only @below-optimal-fear carries two floors, and
# they are the overlap discipline's shared span plus Shapira's residual,
# not one assertion twice, so they stay separate (and two is below W27's
# three-floor threshold).
# 2026-09-17 ground pass: the 17 statements that were premises of some line
# with no line concluding into them now each have one, decided ground by
# ground from the transcript, the reason in a `# ground pass` comment beside
# each. 16 are attributed premise-less floors in the asserting speaker's
# voice (two of them joint: @fear-mobilizes and @crops-transformed, where the
# other speaker agrees on the record). @interp-deployed is the exception: she
# demands the condition and never asserts it, so its line runs from @opaque.
# Two grounds are contested on the record and carry the other speaker's line
# as well ($l-no-humans, $l-feeds), flatly, as he spoke them, which makes the
# I4 notes number 33 and draws the lint's two cross-line W7 by design (two
# opposed floors on one statement are what a contested ground looks like; the
# reasons for not conditioning either are beside the lines). None was
# folded into its consumer: every one is asserted as a claim of its own.
# 65 strengthed lines, every one keyed with a kind by K-SPOKEN as before.
# 2026-09-18, the four flags of step one (AUTHORING_NOTES 2026-09-18): four
# step strengths re-elicited conditional on their now-priced grounds, each
# one class up ($a-coin, $l-slices, $l-covid, $a-market); three lines the
# transcript supports and step one saw ($l-tries, $a-care-route, $l-twenty)
# plus @xrisk-priority conjoined into $l-pause; the 0:50:08 conditional
# docked on $a-glass as a repetition; the @maximizers-sold badge diagnosed
# beside the statement and left; and, by Felix's ruling on the 2026-09-17
# entry's section 10, her grant of the bad branch as her own line at the
# fork ($a-default-doom). 69 strengthed lines, 7 undercut-shaped, I4 still
# 33, the two cross-line W7 unchanged.
# ============================================================

# ---- 1. The doom proposition and the credence dispute ----

@everyone-dies [AI kills everyone]: Artificial superintelligence causes the extinction of humanity. This is the shared subject of the debate. Shapira puts its probability in a ballpark of ten to ninety percent, and Tang declines to put a number on it. [^t001942] [^t012346]  # check: 0.1..0.9 is Shapira's stated ballpark. Tang states no point: her likelihood is flat over the whole board and she calls its mean cosmetic, and she rejects the ten percent he later attributes to her ("I don't think so. No, I really don't think so"). The value her January view shows here is the arithmetic of her mapped lines, never a number she gave. Two speakers, one check slot: the two-author gap, instance 1. In September (2026-09-15) she relays a bound she does not state as her own, the insiders' "more than 10 percent within the next decade" (Hubinger's number; $s-breakwater carries it as its strength, bare, the carried lower bound, with her endorsement of the people behind it as the line's warrant); the same slot's third number, so it stays here: the two-author gap again. The value her September view shows here is derived from that testimony line beside her January lines, and is not a figure she gave · (moved from the gloss 2026-09-26) (id shared with iabied-comprehensive)
  Her reason is that without interpretability the range runs from zero to one hundred percent, and "The interval is the message." When Shapira models her as holding about ten percent, she rejects that. [^t001734] [^t014721]
  In her September 2026 post she relays the lab insiders' warning of odds above ten percent within the decade, and sums up their report as "the centre cannot hold". She states no number of her own. [^p0915-02] [^p0915-03]
  > L: I feel like ten to ninety percent is the ballpark. So what is your ballpark? [^t001942]
  > A: It is from zero percent to one hundred percent. We’re flying blind. We don’t know. So the mean, I guess, is fifty percent, but it’s cosmetic. The interval is the message. [^t001734]
  > A: Well, which is why the variance is so high for me. I literally don’t know. [^t012346]
  > L: I model you as effectively having a P(Doom) that’s, let’s say, ten percent, in the ballpark of ten percent. [^t014650]
  > A: I don’t think so. No, I really don’t think so. [^t014721]
  > S: At this rate, the centre cannot hold. [^p0915-03]

@opaque [Frontier transformer models are opaque]: Frontier transformer models can be measured inside but not reliably interpreted. Tang calls them "wooden Trojan horses that we literally don't know what's inside". Her case against putting a number on doom rests on this. [^t001734] [^t002043]  # (moved from the gloss 2026-09-26) (id shared with iabied-comprehensive; here asserted from Tang's own interpretability case; shared ground for $a-nan and $a-material-uc, so it stays a top-level head)
  In her September 2026 post she calls the all-powerful systems expected to do everything "hard to interpret". [^p0915-08]
  > A: we can measure some of the internals, but we cannot reliably interpret them [^t001734]
  > A: so not the current wooden Trojan horses that we literally don’t know what’s inside, whether it’s going to do a sharp left turn or maybe a sharp right turn, you don’t know [^t002043]
  > S: hard to interpret [^p0915-08]
  $a-blur [A: self-attention blurs cause, so models stay opaque] 0.9? @opaque: Tang asserts that the transformer's own architecture keeps today's frontier models opaque. Quadratic self-attention "literally is a blur of what causes what", so nobody knows where a model hides its intentions, or whether it hides any. [^t005008]  # kind: mechanism
    She contrasts it with older architectures such as RNNs and LSTMs, which were much easier to inspect and steer. [^t005008]
    > A: I think a lot of the current muddiness is because of the quadratic self-attention transformer architecture, which literally is a blur of what causes what. [^t005008]
    > A: And so because of this, we don’t even know where the plane is actually hiding its intentions or whether it’s hiding its intentions. [^t005008]

@priceable [A meaningful credence on AI doom is assignable today]: One can responsibly state a number or range for P(doom) with today's interpretability. Shapira says yes, since some estimates are clearly wrong and a ballpark such as ten to ninety percent is a real statement. [^t001837] [^t001942]  # audrey: NaN [^t001734]; liron: clearly yes [^t001837]
  Tang says no. Without real interpretability her P(doom) is "NaN, or Not A Number": her range runs from zero to one hundred percent, and "The interval is the message." She would give "a real number" once systems that can be seen into are a condition of deployment. [^t001734] [^t002043]
  It unfolds into three cases. Tang's case is against a number, Shapira's is for a ballpark, and the third names the condition under which she would give one.
  > A: My P(Doom) is NaN, or Not A Number, and here’s why. [^t001734]
  # Three single-voice batteries, one declared box each (D58): her case
  # against assignability, his case for a ballpark anyway, and the
  # condition under which she would price it. The slicing support and
  # $a-glass are left as independent factors deliberately: disjoint
  # mechanisms (his slicing works TODAY; hers is conditional on
  # @interp-deployed), so the overlap discipline does not collapse them.
  # @oom-slices is homed at TOP LEVEL below (burial test: $l-material in
  # the next cluster consumes it too).
  ::nan-case [A: why she will not give a number]: Tang argues that no meaningful probability of doom can be given today. She treats risk as capability divided by visibility, and today's architecture leaves the visibility term missing.
    She adds that the doom claim will probably not be settled within her lifetime.
    > A: we’re trying to compute a value where the inspection term is missing, like dividing by zero or something [^t001734]
    @risk-needs-vis [Risk assessment requires visibility]: Assessing a risk requires visibility into the system that poses it. Tang's working model is that risk is capability divided by visibility. With the inspection term missing, the division is undefined, "like dividing by zero or something". [^t001734]
      > A: If you think of risk as capability divided by visibility, the story looks simple, right? The numerator is climbing fast. Everyone sees it climb. [^t001734]
      $a-nuclear [A: nuclear risk is priceable because it is visible] 0.8? @risk-needs-vis: Asked about nuclear war, Tang treats it as the contrast case, where risk can be estimated. There the path to disaster is visible, because "somebody has to launch that nuclear missile", so her estimate is "much more standard shaped". [^t002115]  # kind: analogy
        When Shapira asks for a number, she puts a nuclear war that halves the population by 2100 at roughly fifty percent, with a narrower spread than her estimate for AI. [^t002150] [^t002115]
        > A: I think for nuclear, it’s much more interpretable because somebody has to launch that nuclear missile. And so my P(Doom) for nuclear is much more standard shaped. So yeah, my nuclear variance is quite narrower. [^t002115]
        > A: Yeah, so I think I’ll put it roughly around fifty percent, and— [^t002150]
    $a-nan [A: without interpretability, P(doom) is not a number] 0.9? ~@priceable | @opaque AND @risk-needs-vis: Tang argues that opaque models leave no meaningful number to give. Risk needs visibility, and without interpretability the likelihood is a flat line covering the whole board, from zero to one hundred percent. [^t001734]  # kind: deductive
      In her words, "the mean, I guess, is fifty percent, but it's cosmetic. The interval is the message. The calculation simply does not converge unless you have real interpretability". [^t001734]
      > A: But if the likelihood function is broken, it literally looks like a flat line, right? It covers the entire board. [^t001734]
      > A: The calculation simply does not converge unless you have real interpretability. [^t001734]
    @unverifiable-epoch [The doom claim can't be settled in our horizon]: The doom claim cannot be settled within our own time horizon. Tang compares it to a coin flipped into outer space: "by the time it lands, I'm probably not here anymore". [^t001905]
      > A: Okay, but it’s flipping into outer space. By the time it lands, I’m probably not here anymore. [^t001905]
      # ground pass 2026-09-17: (a) floor. She asserts it as a claim of her own, by likeness; "probably" is her hedge (RS4). Shapira contests the inference drawn from it ("that's an even easier question", the target of $a-coin), never the ground.
      $a-outer-space [A: the coin lands after we are gone] 0.75? @unverifiable-epoch: Tang asserts it by analogy with a coin flipped into outer space. The coin is still spinning, and by the time it lands she is "probably not here anymore". The claim is about her own lifetime, and the "probably" is hers. [^t001905]  # kind: analogy
        > A: So this is like flipping a coin into outer space. [^t001905]
    # re-elicited 2026-09-18 conditional on its ground (AUTHORING_NOTES 2026-09-18, item 1): the July 0.7? (RS5) read the whole turn's hedging, and the turn's "probably" is the ground's ("I'm probably not here anymore", priced on $a-outer-space since 2026-09-17). Granted the ground, what is left on the step is its delivery: an exploratory opener ("Well, I mean, I don't know, right?") and a rhetorical question, one hedge's worth (RS4). The "probably" inside her question is his claimant's, quoted back at him.
    $a-coin [A: nothing settles the bet, so no range can be ruled out] 0.75? ~@priceable | @unverifiable-epoch AND $l-slices: Tang answers Shapira's case for a ballpark with a coin flipped into outer space. If nothing will settle the bet in our time, she asks, "what position do I have to say that they're probably wrong?", even about someone who puts doom below one in a million. [^t001905]  # kind: testimony
      > A: So what position do I have to say that they’re probably wrong? [^t001905]
  ::ballpark-case [L: why a ballpark is assignable anyway]: Shapira argues that a ballpark for doom can be given anyway. Slicing probabilities by orders of magnitude of odds, with background risks such as asteroid impacts as a floor, makes ten to ninety percent a meaningful statement.
    > L: I mean, there’s clearly a ballpark. I feel like ten to ninety percent is the ballpark. [^t001942]
    @asteroid-floor [Background risks set a meaningful floor]: Known background risks set a floor under how small a doom estimate can sensibly be. Shapira's reference point is that "once you get to one in a hundred million, you're just talking about yearly asteroid impacts", so a P(doom) below one in a million is clearly wrong. [^t001942]
      > L: I mean, once you get to one in a hundred million, you’re just talking about yearly asteroid impacts, right? [^t001942]
      # ground pass 2026-09-17: (a) floor. His own claim with a cited base rate; "I sure as hell know" is categorical (RS1). Tang answers "it's spinning" and never contests the floor. (Corrected 2026-09-26: she never addresses the asteroid base rate, but her 0:20:43 "It's zero to one hundred" keeps values below one in a million inside her range, so she does not grant the floor's consequence either; the line stays his, flat, as he spoke it.)
      $l-asteroid [L: past one in a hundred million it is asteroid odds] 0.9? @asteroid-floor: Shapira grounds the floor in a known base rate, the yearly odds of an asteroid impact. At one in a hundred million, he says, "you're just talking about yearly asteroid impacts". [^t001942]  # kind: empirical
        He cannot say whether the odds are twenty or twenty-five to one, but he is sure P(doom) is above one in a million. [^t001942]
        > L: I can’t really tell you if it’s twenty to one, twenty-five to one, but I sure as hell know that the P(Doom) is more than a million to one against. [^t001942]
    # re-elicited 2026-09-18 conditional on its grounds (AUTHORING_NOTES 2026-09-18, item 1): the July 0.85? (RS2) was the turn's register with the slicing and the floor unpriced; both are floors of his since 2026-09-17.
